findings.reasoning: Hypothesis: a low-privileged BackWPup role can modify onboarding backup jobs through `admin-post.php?action=backwpup` even though that role does not have job-edit or settings privileges. Trace: `BackWPup_Admin::save_post_form()` only checks the page nonce and `current_user_can('backwpup')` at `inc/class-admin.php:838-852`. When `$_POST['page'] === 'backwpup'` and `$_POST['onboarding'] === '1'`, it dispatches directly into `BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form()` at `inc/class-admin.php:892-895`. The onboarding UI is reachable while `backwpup_onboarding` is true through a submenu that requires only `backwpup_backups` (`inc/class-admin.php:658-667`), and its form posts a `backwpup_page` nonce plus hidden `onboarding=1` to `admin-post.php` (`plugins/backwpup/pages/onboarding.php:14-20`, `plugins/backwpup/components/containers/form-start.php:40-46`). The bundled `backwpup_check` role explicitly has `backwpup` and `backwpup_backups` but lacks `backwpup_jobs_edit` and `backwpup_settings` (`inc/class-install.php:142-158`), so the weaker top-level gate is materially broader than the intended privilege boundary. The shipped 'backwpup_check' role has 'backwpup=true' but not 'backwpup_jobs_edit' or 'backwpup_settings' [inc/class-install.php:142-177]. Inside getblock(), attacker-controlled 'block_type' may be 'children' and attacker-controlled 'block_name' is passed to BackWPupHelpersAdapter::children() [src/Frontend/API/Rest.php:91-99]; the helper only blocks traversal and then includes any file under 'parts/' [inc/Utils/BackWPupHelpers.php:72-109]. Requesting 'block_name=sidebar/storage-FTP' returns a form whose password field is prefilled with BackWPup_Encryption::decrypt( BackWPup_Option::get( $job_id, 'ftppass' ) ) [parts/sidebar/storage-FTP.php:170-179].
